deal_summary: The project moved through technical and price choices for a filling line; by late December one line was described as nearing production readiness, while acceptance, warranty timing, and related scope questions were still being discussed (evidence: 0-7).

customer_need.summary: The manager worklog records a filling and labeling line for a paint-like product in PET containers; customer calls confirm discussion of multiple container formats, changeover, filling layout, and labeling (evidence: 0-1,5-6). Detailed baseline specifications are manager-recorded rather than independently repeated by the customer.

deal_dynamics.early: A manager note records the initial line requirements; in a later call the parties compared one versus multiple container setups, changeover time, and cost (evidence: 0-1).
deal_dynamics.middle: The customer said samples and marketing inputs were not yet ready, then discussed the added feed-hopper cost and the need to consult an engineer; a lower-cost linear option was also reviewed (evidence: 2-4).
deal_dynamics.late: The customer said the carousel layout was preferred and clarified marking needs; on Dec 24 the manager described one line as nearly ready, while the customer raised site readiness, acceptance, and warranty-start questions (evidence: 5-7).

positive_signals: The customer engaged in detailed configuration and maintenance discussions and stated a preference for the carousel arrangement (evidence: 1,4-5).
The customer clarified that marking was needed on the bucket and discussed possible future integration (evidence: 6).
negative_signals: On Nov 11 the customer said sample and marketing inputs were not yet available, delaying final technical definition (evidence: 2).
customer_behavior.initiative: The customer discussed packaging and changeover alternatives, said it would consult its chief engineer, selected the carousel direction, and raised practical acceptance and warranty questions (evidence: 1,3,5,7).
customer_behavior.decision_process: The call record refers to marketing and engineering input on requirements; later discussion involved a director, customer colleagues, and legal review around inspection and warranty timing (evidence: 2-3,5,7).

strong_actions: Presented alternative configurations and cost paths, followed up on technical requirements, and shared a production-readiness estimate for one line (evidence: 1,4,7).
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: Technical and commercial questions were revisited across the period; at the late stage, acceptance and warranty-start concerns still needed clarification (evidence: 3-7).
manager_behavior.next_step_control: The carousel direction and marking scope were clearer, but customer sample/design inputs for related scope and the acceptance, warranty, and site-readiness plan remained open (evidence: 2,5-7).

turning_points.description: The customer reported that sample and marketing information was not yet ready, leaving the project in a theoretical scoping phase.
The customer stated a preference to retain the carousel layout while continuing to consider feed and package-handling details.
One line was described as nearly ready, while the customer asked about acceptance timing, site readiness, and when warranty would begin.

primary_trajectory_explanation.explanation: The visible record shows gradual narrowing of the equipment configuration and substantial technical discussion. A line was later described as nearing readiness, but customer-side input, site readiness, acceptance, and warranty timing remained relevant dependencies; this does not establish the final commercial outcome (evidence: 2-7).

secondary_factors: Packaging samples and marketing requirements delayed early technical definition (evidence: 2).
Several related equipment scopes appear in the late call, so progress on one should not be treated as resolution of every discussed scope (evidence: 7).

what_could_be_done: Confirm the acceptance plan and warranty-start condition in writing before dispatch, and maintain a dated checklist of customer sample and design inputs for remaining scope.
limits: Customer marketing and engineering decisions, customer site readiness, and production specifications were outside the manager's sole control (evidence: 2-3,5,7).
The view does not show whether these open points changed the eventual outcome.

evidence.paraphrase: Manager worklog records a paint-like product, PET containers, target throughput, and filling/labeling equipment requirements; detailed specifications are manager-reported.
The call compared one versus multiple container formats, changeover time, and cost; the customer said the discussed changeover duration was acceptable and asked to compare cost.
The customer said samples and marketing decisions were still pending and promised to provide new information when available.
The parties discussed an added feed-hopper option estimated at about 1.5 million rubles; the customer said it would review the option with its chief engineer.
The manager outlined price-reduction options including a linear configuration; the customer asked about cleaning and servicing the peristaltic dosing unit.
The customer said the carousel configuration would be retained and continued discussing layout and how to handle potentially leaking packages.
The customer clarified that the label would go on the bucket rather than its lid and asked about future integration of a marker or applicator.

The manager described one line as nearly ready; the customer discussed delayed acceptance, site readiness, and concern about warranty starting before installation, while another line scope still needed preliminary design inputs.

uncertainties: The previous preprocessing role gave me prior raw-timeline chronology familiarity, including awareness that lifecycle-boundary content required conservative treatment; this limits chronology blindness even though no outcome label was consulted.
The detailed opening specifications come from a manager worklog, not direct customer speech in the retained events.
The late conversation covers more than one equipment scope; progress on one should not be assumed to apply to all of them.
